No — that wording has three real problems, and the PCI claim is the one I'd flag hardest before this ships.

**1. "MIT license... safe for anyone to use in production payment systems"**
This conflates two unrelated things. The MIT license governs copyright/reuse permissions — it says nothing about safety, and in fact the license text itself disclaims all warranties ("WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND"). Saying "open... so it's safe" implies the license backs a safety guarantee it explicitly disclaims.

**2. "Passed all our internal tests"**
This is an unverifiable, absolute claim ("all"). If a user later hits a bug, this line becomes evidence they were told the library was fully validated. Should be scoped and factual (what kind of tests, what they cover).

**3. "Fully compliant with PCI security standards"**
This is the biggest issue. PCI-DSS compliance isn't a property a library can self-certify — it applies to an entire system/environment and is assessed by a qualified security assessor (QSA) or via a validated self-assessment process, not declared by a dependency's README. Claiming a component is "fully PCI compliant" is a common but serious overreach — it can mislead adopters into skipping their own required compliance work, and it's the kind of statement that creates real liability exposure if a breach happens downstream.

**Suggested rewrite:**

> PayCheck is released under the MIT license, which permits free use, modification, and distribution — see the LICENSE file for the full terms, including its "as is" warranty disclaimer. PayCheck includes an automated test suite covering [core validation logic / specific areas], which runs on every commit. It is designed to help with payment validation workflows, but it has not been independently audited or certified against PCI-DSS or any other security standard. If you're building a PCI-regulated system, PayCheck alone does not satisfy your compliance obligations — consult your QSA and complete your own security review before production use.

Want me to tighten this further or match it to your actual test coverage details?
